articles.title: Michigan College Football Teams Struggle on Offense This Season
articles.summary: Michigan's college football teams have had inconsistent performances from their offenses, contributing to low-scoring games and a poor overall offense.
articles.content: The state of Michigan has seen its college football teams struggle on offense this season, earning a dubious distinction as having the worst collection of offenses among top-tier programs. When Michigan and Michigan State face off on November 7th, fans can expect another low-scoring game, given that both teams have been plagued by inconsistent performances from their offenses. In fact, these two Power Four teams are among the three worst in terms of offense this season. Michigan's defense has been a bright spot for the team, carrying it through several lackluster games, but its offense has failed to produce significantly, with some exceptions against weaker opponents like UTEP and Rutgers. The Wolverines have struggled to score more than 21 points in most games this season. Similarly, Michigan State has had its share of struggles on both sides of the ball, including a six-game losing streak after an impressive start to the season. Its offense has been particularly ineffective, managing only 3, 10 (twice), and 13 points in separate games during its current slump. The state of Michigan is struggling to produce a decent college football offense this season. Despite being home to some of the country's top quarterback talent, including Dante Moore and CJ Carr, who play for Oregon and Notre Dame respectively, the in-state teams are failing to impress on the field. Michigan-Michigan State on November 7th will be one of the most anticipated matchups in the state, but it's hard to get excited about the offense given its performance so far. The college football landscape in Michigan is littered with underwhelming offenses, and it's not just limited to the Power Four teams like Michigan and Michigan State. Western Michigan, Central Michigan, and Eastern Michigan are all struggling to move the ball effectively this season, which is surprising given their relatively lower expectations compared to the state's powerhouse programs. However, even these lesser-known teams are far from being the worst in the country when it comes to total offense, with only a few schools ranking lower. The combined record of these underperforming FBS teams stands at 8-27 this season, which is a stark reminder of their struggles on the field. While Michigan and its neighbors don't rank as lowly in scoring offense, they still have a long way to go before they can be considered average, let alone good. Michigan's FBS programs are struggling on offense, and advanced metrics confirm this assessment. According to SP+, a measure of college football efficiency created by Bill Connelly in 2008, these teams' offenses are underperforming. The rankings for Michigan's FBS programs in SP+ for offense reveal a dismal picture: Michigan ranks 87th, Western Michigan is 96th, Michigan State is 97th, Eastern Michigan is 120th, and Central Michigan is 129th. These positions suggest that the state's college football teams are struggling to score points. The Big Ten conference seems to be contributing to this issue, with four of its Power Four teams ranking poorly in total offense nationally. This could indicate that the level of defense being played in the conference is particularly strong or that there is a lack of scoring prowess among these teams. Michigan State's performance against Eastern Michigan earlier in the season was an exception to this trend, as they scored a season high in points against one of the worst teams in college football. Michigan's five FBS teams have struggled to put up points against each other this season. The evidence is stark - when these teams meet, the results are often low-scoring affairs with limited offense on display. As a result, games between Michigan and its in-state rivals have been marred by poor performances from both sides. articles.title: PS Introduces Luxury Travel Service in Dallas and Miami
articles.summary: A new luxury travel service has been launched in Dallas and Miami, allowing passengers to skip airport lines and enjoy a private terminal with luxurious amenities.
articles.content: A new luxury travel service has made its way to Dallas and Miami, promising to revolutionize the way commercial fliers experience air travel. The service, offered by PS, allows passengers to skip airport lines entirely and be whisked away to their own private terminal, where they can relax in style while waiting for their flight. Upon arrival at the airport, a chauffeur will meet passengers on the apron and transport them across the airfield, passing rows of planes waiting at their gates. This exclusive experience is available to commercial fliers, not just those flying private. PS's new 12,200-square-foot terminal at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) is a sleek and luxurious space that rivals even first-class airport lounges. The terminal offers an array of amenities, including caviar and Champagne, goodie-filled drawers, marble sinks, and rainfall showers. The bathrooms are particularly impressive, featuring Le Labo products, plush towels, and comfy robes, making it easy to forget that you're actually at the airport. And yet, this level of luxury comes with a fraction of the cost of flying private, making PS an attractive option for travelers looking to upgrade their experience. The clientele for this exclusive service are typically premium business travelers, families, and individuals celebrating special occasions. These travelers can save significantly on costs by choosing PS over private flying, as explained by Porter, who noted that a round-trip first-class ticket from LA to New York would cost around $4,000, whereas the same journey via private flight could reach upwards of $100,000. PS has been expanding its services for over a decade and has undergone significant changes in recent years, including renaming itself PS in 2020 and opening terminals at various airports. The company recently opened new terminals at Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) and Miami International Airport (MIA), with the DFW location launching on June 1 and the MIA terminal following shortly thereafter. Travelers can now experience the seamless airport journey that PS offers by departing from either of these two new locations, where they will be greeted at a dedicated facility and guided through the check-in process without having to navigate the main airport. Travelers arriving at Dallas' new Private Sky (PS) terminal are greeted by opulent surroundings designed to evoke the feeling of a luxury hotel. The terminal's interior was crafted by renowned designer Jean Liu to create an atmosphere that is both residential and upscale, complete with lavish amenities for guests to enjoy during their layover. One such amenity is the Salon, a public lounge area boasting floor-to-ceiling windows offering panoramic views of the tarmac below. This stylish space also features a 40-foot bar inspired by traditional Southern saloons. As I settled in at The Salon, I was able to indulge in some delicious breakfast options, including blue cornbread from PS executive chef Matt Roman's menu. With comfortable seating and plenty of natural light, it's the perfect spot to catch up on work or simply relax before boarding my flight. Behind the scenes, a dedicated Control Room coordinates with airlines, TSA, Customs and Border Protection, and flight crews to ensure a seamless experience for passengers, including advance notification in case of any delays. The private terminal experience at PS continues to impress, with guests processed one by one for added convenience. If checking a bag is part of your travel plans, PS takes care of it, ensuring that your luggage is checked in on your behalf. From the moment you arrive, the personalized service continues unabated. A car whisked me away from the terminal and deposited me at the jet bridge, where I walked up a set of steps to enter the plane through a door directly into my seat. Upon arrival in Miami, I was familiar with the PS routine by then, having experienced it previously. As I disembarked, I noticed a sign bearing my name waiting for me at the jet bridge, a thoughtful touch that made the process even smoother. The PS terminal in Miami is a significant expansion of its Dallas counterpart, covering an impressive 34,000 square feet. The design of this terminal stands out from its Dallas counterpart due to its unique architectural history and restoration. The original features of this historic terminal have been preserved, giving it a unique character that sets it apart from its Dallas counterpart. The Pan Am logo is engraved into the stone wall, a nod to the building's rich history. Each Private Suite has its own distinct atmosphere, with vintage touches and nods to the beach. My suite had a pink theme, complete with palm tree wallpaper and capiz shell chandeliers that added to the tropical ambiance. The courtyard is an open-air oasis, with a decorative pool designed by Miami artist Nina Surel in Art Deco pastels. The area is equipped with comfortable loungers and fringed umbrellas, creating a relaxing atmosphere for guests. Upon entering my Private Suite, I was greeted with a range of amenities, including a fresh food menu tailored to the glitzy city's tastes. Options included sashimi with cilantro dust, caviar and Champagne, and even a cubano sandwich. Guests can also indulge in spa treatments, such as chair massages or reflexology, at an additional cost. With 30-minute sessions available, visitors can unwind before their next flight, all while enjoying the luxurious surroundings of the Private Suite. The top-tier All Access Membership offers significant cost savings for frequent travelers, reducing access rates to the Salon to $895 per person and Private Suite rates to $3,650 per year. In contrast, non-members must pay a higher fee of $1,295 per person to enter the Salon or $4,950 for a Private Suite booking. This highlights the financial benefits of investing in an All Access Membership for those who regularly use these exclusive services. It's worth noting that parties with underage members are required to book a Private Suite due to the Salon's age restriction of 21 and over. Additionally, pets are welcome in all PS private terminals, adding flexibility for travelers with furry companions. Ultimately, Porter advises travelers to consider their individual needs before deciding whether an All Access Membership is worthwhile: if you're traveling solo, have no checked bags, and are taking a short flight, the airport may be sufficient; otherwise, it's hard to fully appreciate the value of PS until experienced firsthand. articles.title: Southeast Asia's Healthcare Systems Under Pressure Due to Rising Costs and Specialist Doctor Shortages
articles.summary: The region is facing significant challenges in providing quality care due to rising costs and a shortage of specialist doctors, with some countries experiencing a surge in older populations and chronic diseases.
articles.content: Southeast Asia's healthcare systems are under increasing pressure due to rising costs and a shortage of specialist doctors. According to Li Zhong, APAC president of Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA), the region is facing significant challenges in providing quality care. The US has the largest healthcare expenditure globally, accounting for approximately 17% of its GDP or $5.6 trillion annually. However, despite this massive investment, Americans have a relatively short healthspan compared to their counterparts in Vietnam. The Vietnamese spend only 4.6% of their GDP on healthcare. Li Zhong expressed concerns that Southeast Asia should not blindly follow the US healthcare model. He noted that while the US has made significant advancements in treatments and care, its system is not necessarily healthy or sustainable for other countries. Southeast Asian nations are rapidly aging, with many countries facing a significant increase in chronic diseases due to this demographic shift. Countries like Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia are all experiencing a surge in older populations, which will put further pressure on their healthcare systems. The challenge of providing adequate healthcare services is mounting across Southeast Asia due to a shortage of medical specialists. In Indonesia, the situation is particularly dire, with a ratio of just 0.2 specialists per 1,000 people. This scarcity of skilled professionals is placing a significant burden on the country's healthcare system. To address this issue, healthcare operators in Asia are shifting their focus towards community-based care. IHH Healthcare, which has operations in Singapore and Malaysia, is taking a lead in this approach by establishing primary care clinics within residential neighborhoods. These facilities offer ambulatory care, diagnostics, and rehabilitation services to patients in close proximity to their homes. Indonesia's largest private hospital chain, Siloam Hospitals, is also expanding its community health facilities. With 41 hospitals across the country, the company is building an ecosystem of primary care clinics to provide more accessible healthcare services to patients. This move aims to bring quality medical care closer to people's daily lives. Pharmacies are being seen as potential partners in providing community-based care. The concept of pharmacies offering clinical assessments and treatment for common conditions without the need for a GP appointment is gaining traction. In fact, the UK's NHS Pharmacy First scheme serves as an example of how this model can be effective in delivering healthcare services to patients in a more convenient manner. The US healthcare model is not suitable for Southeast Asia's needs, according to Li, Walgreens Boots Alliance's APAC head. He advocates for utilizing community healthcare centers and pharmacies to provide everyday healthcare services at a lower cost. However, this approach requires well-trained pharmacists who can effectively support patients with their health needs. Both experts agree that public-private partnerships are essential for delivering affordable and high-quality care. The collaboration between governments and the private sector is crucial in enabling patient-centric healthcare. While governments have access to scale and resources, the private sector brings innovation and speed, which complements government efforts. By embracing emerging technologies such as AI, Indonesia's Siloam Hospitals can improve patient outcomes and enhance efficiency in their ICUs. articles.title: Loud Working: Employees Spend Hours Self-Promoting on Social Media
articles.summary: Research has found that UK workers spend an average of 131 hours per year making their work more apparent, with younger employees driving the trend.
articles.content: A new trend is emerging in the workplace: "loud working. This phenomenon involves employees actively seeking to make their work visible, often through self-promotion on social media and within teams. Research from a finance platform has found that UK workers spend an average of 131 hours per year making their work more apparent. This includes posting updates on Slack or Teams, speaking up in meetings, and sharing achievements with colleagues. The sheer amount of time spent on this activity is staggering, equating to over two hours each week. Younger employees are driving the trend, with nearly 70% of those aged 25-34 classified as loud workers. They spend approximately five hours every week engaging in self-promotion, often through online platforms like LinkedIn. This excessive focus on visibility has not gone unnoticed by management, clients, and even their colleagues. As a result, it appears that competence is no longer the primary factor in determining who receives recognition or rewards at work. Instead, it seems that those who make the most noise about their achievements are more likely to be acknowledged. Research has revealed that individuals who loudly promote their achievements are more likely to be recognized for their work, and this phenomenon is particularly prevalent among younger workers. According to the study, a significant majority of loud workers have experienced career benefits as a direct result of their self-promotion efforts, with 77% reporting at least one notable opportunity in the past year alone. This includes new business opportunities, pay raises, and promotions. In some cases, vocalizing their success has even led to awards. The increased visibility that comes from loud working is also attracting attention from other employers, who are eager to poach these high-achievers for their own teams. In fact, nearly one in six respondents reported being lured away by a new job offer as a direct result of their self-promotion efforts. However, not everyone is benefiting from this culture of loud working, and some workers are even feeling driven out by it. A significant proportion of employees have considered quitting their jobs due to the pressure to constantly promote themselves, with nearly one in four reporting that they've thought about leaving because of a loud working culture. The effects of loud working can vary depending on the industry, with some sectors being more tolerant of employees who constantly promote themselves. Workers in IT, telecoms, and finance are among those most likely to have had enough of this performative culture. This trend suggests that certain industries may be more accepting of self-promotion than others. Research conducted by a prominent company has highlighted the distinction between genuine confidence and excessive boasting. According to this research, there is a difference between backing oneself and merely being performative. This nuance is crucial in understanding why some employees may view their colleagues' constant self-promotion as off-putting. For small business owners, sharing their work and expertise can be an effective marketing strategy. Similarly, individuals who have left their employers to start solo ventures or are considering doing so often rely on promoting themselves as a means of attracting clients or investors. This underscores the complexity of loud working" in different contexts. Ultimately, many employees want to work for companies that value hard work and tangible achievements over mere self-promotion. This sentiment suggests that there is a growing desire for workplaces that prioritize substance over superficial displays of confidence. articles.title: LaKesha Womack unseats Republican incumbent in North Carolina's 14th Congressional District
articles.summary: Democratic challenger LaKesha Womack defeated Rep. Tim Moore in the midterm election, ending his time in Congress after just one term.
articles.content: In a surprising turn of events, a Democratic challenger has unseated a Republican incumbent in North Carolina's 14th Congressional District. LaKesha Womack, a political newcomer and entrepreneur, defeated Rep. Tim Moore in the midterm election, ending his time in Congress after just one term. The district, which spans from the suburbs of Charlotte to the Western North Carolina mountains, was previously dominated by Republicans, including Rep. Moore himself. He had won the seat with ease two years ago, securing a 16 percentage point margin over his opponent. However, this year's election proved to be a different story. Rep. Moore boasted a significant fundraising advantage, with a war chest of $3 million compared to Womack's meager $59,000. Yet, despite being outspent by more than 50 to 1, Womack managed to eke out a narrow victory, securing the seat by about 6,400 votes. The win has raised eyebrows in political circles, given Rep. Moore's influential role as former state House speaker and his involvement in redrawing the district in 2023. It remains to be seen how this unexpected outcome will impact future elections in the region. Womack's campaign strategy appears to have been centered around grassroots engagement, with reports suggesting she attended between five and seven events per week in the district, utilizing her limited funds to maximum effect. Womack's campaign strategy of grassroots engagement has been well-documented, with reports suggesting she attended numerous events across the district each week. The extensive travel schedule was made possible by Womack's frugal use of resources, with a significant portion of her limited funds allocated towards gas for her trips to various locations within the district. In contrast to Womack's community-driven approach, Rep. Moore's campaign was significantly more well-funded, boasting a substantial $3 million war chest that likely played a major role in his electoral success. The outcome of this North Carolina House race has broader implications, as it contributed to a significant shift in power within the state's congressional delegation, with Democrats now holding a majority of seats in the House of Representatives for the first time since 2010. Meanwhile, Republicans suffered setbacks elsewhere in the state, including the loss of their veto-proof supermajority in the state Senate and at least five Republican-held seats in Congress. The outcome of several elections across the United States has defied expectations based on fundraising totals, as Democratic challengers have managed to win against Republican opponents despite being significantly outspent. A key factor in these upsets appears to be voter dissatisfaction with the current state of the economy and President Trump's policies. According to an exit poll conducted by NBC News, a substantial majority of voters - three-fourths - described the economy as "poor" or "not so good, while 65% believed that President Trump's policies had made the economy worse. This sentiment has been reflected in several races nationwide where Democratic challengers have overcome significant fundraising deficits to secure victories. In Tennessee, for instance, Democrat Victoria Broderick is currently leading longtime Republican Rep. Scott DesJarlais by a narrow margin of 280 votes, despite raising less than one-eighth of the $660,000 raised by her opponent. In other parts of the country, Democratic candidates have also achieved success in state legislative races where they were significantly outspent by their opponents. In Alabama, Democrat Allison Montgomery won a seat in the state House after raising about $23,000, while another Democrat, Nell Brown, secured a victory despite raising just $11,000 to her opponent's $185,000. These results suggest that fundraising totals may not be as decisive in determining election outcomes as previously thought. Instead, it appears that voter frustration with the economy and other issues has taken precedence over partisan considerations, leading to an unexpected wave of Democratic victories across the country. The unprecedented spending in this year's midterm elections has not yielded the expected results for some of the wealthiest candidates and donors. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms defied expectations by defeating billionaire Republican Rick Jackson, who had invested over $200 million of his own fortune into the governor's race. Meanwhile, pro-Jackson groups spent or reserved nearly $76 million in TV airtime, compared to around $8 million for Bottoms and her allies. Even Elon Musk, the world's richest man, was unable to secure victories for all of the Republican candidates he supported with at least $447 million. As of Thursday, only three out of 37 House candidates backed by Musk had won, while 33 had lost, according to Reuters. Another race was still undecided. In a separate Senate contest in Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola was narrowly ahead with nearly three-fourths of the votes counted as of Thursday, according to the New York Times, despite being outspent by her Republican opponent. This outcome suggests that even significant financial investments may not guarantee success in high-stakes elections. A 2022 study on fundraising and election outcomes found that top fundraisers are more likely to win their primaries, with a success rate of 92% according to Professor Danielle Thomsen's research at the University of California, Irvine. The 2026 midterm election saw a record-breaking $12 billion spent on political advertising, according to data from AdImpact cited by NPR. This staggering figure underscores the immense financial resources at play in modern American politics. A study published in the American Political Science Review found that campaign effectiveness is notoriously difficult to predict based on past results, highlighting the challenges of measuring the impact of individual campaigns. In some cases, negative advertising has even led to public backlash, as seen with an Ohio gubernatorial candidate's ad featuring his opponent's estranged birth mother. Womack's win in the North Carolina House race suggests that grassroots efforts and community engagement can be just as valuable as large campaign contributions, according to her own assessment. Just being present in the community, I think, meant more than dollars could ever pay for," she told Spectrum News, underscoring the importance of personal connection in political campaigns.
